subject.title: feat(gateway): pre-handshake WS verifyClient with Sec-Fetch-Site and forwarded-header hardening

question: Should OpenClaw permanently expose these three opt-in `gateway.security.*` WebSocket/proxy hardening controls now, or should their policy and naming be folded into the existing Gateway origin-policy work first?
rationale: This creates a public persisted configuration contract across Gateway origin, proxy, and browser-upgrade behavior; source review can assess the implementation but cannot choose the long-term product boundary.

options.title: Approve the scoped opt-in contract
options.body: Keep the three default-off settings, after current-head live proof confirms their stated proxy and browser compatibility boundaries.

options.title: Consolidate with origin-policy work
options.body: Pause this PR and define one maintainer-owned Gateway origin/proxy policy contract with the related open work before adding new settings.

options.title: Land only a narrower internal seam
options.body: Retain a generic pre-handshake hook but defer the operator-facing enforcement toggles until the permanent policy is decided.

recommendation.title: Consolidate with origin-policy work
recommendation.body: Pause this PR and define one maintainer-owned Gateway origin/proxy policy contract with the related open work before adding new settings.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR discussion directly identifies this person as the requested decision maker for gate placement and configuration naming.
